mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive or not significantly different from baseline when GDPC1 declines by more than -0.5% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and increases recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 5-year averages signals a high-inflation, high-rate regime, which erodes real corporate earnings and increases discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 5-year averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals synchronized demand expansion, which boosts earnings growth and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both rise for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1 and HOUST both rise for three consecutive months in an early-cycle regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals robust labor market tightening, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-mo moving average AND UNRATE stable (change < 0.1pp)
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month moving average and UNRATE is stable.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a broad-based supply recovery, which increases earnings visibility and reduces risk premia, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-mo moving average for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during six consecutive months where INDPRO remains above its 12-month moving average.
